rule: Planner tools key, read through the frontmatter reader CHECK 16 uses, is exactly ten named tools, and its frontmatter contains no Write, Edit or Bash
description: plugin/agents/cerebrate.md is the planner. Its frontmatter tools: list is what grants it tools, so this fixture pins that list. The set_check reads the top-level tools key with extract_frontmatter_key, which runs check16_collect_entries, the frontmatter reader CHECK 16 uses in tools/policy_check.sh, and requires, in equal mode with expected_counts, exactly these ten tools, each once: Read, Glob, Grep, LSP, WebSearch, WebFetch and the four claude-mem search tools. A tool added in any form the reader reads fails as an extra: a block list at any indent, a compact list, an inline flow list, a comma-separated string, or a second tools key. Each entry is compared whole, so Bash(...) is not Bash and fails as an extra; a duplicated tool fails its count, and a deleted tool fails as missing. A deleted list fails as ten missing tools. A tools value in a form the reader cannot read fails the check and names the file, line and text: a quoted or indented key, a block scalar, an unclosed flow sequence, the key's text on any other frontmatter line, or an entry outside the tool-entry grammar. set_check is used because an added grant is the threat, and a presence pin can only notice deletion. The three frontmatter-absent consumers require that the substrings Write, Edit and Bash appear nowhere in the frontmatter. A Bash(...) entry grants the whole Bash tool, so the Bash consumer is what keeps the planner without a shell. The source pin sits on the Do Not item that forbids writing, editing, creating, or deleting files; deleting that item is loud. What this fixture does not check: (a) what each listed tool can do; the pin claims names, never capability or meaning; (b) grants from any other file, such as settings files, hooks, or the delegation that starts the planner; (c) any other agent file; files is a literal list that names only cerebrate.md and is blind to newly added files.

source.pattern: write, edit, create, or delete files
